input: Build a simple wooden step stool for the kitchen

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of steps and the height of the stool changes the complexity of the build, the amount of materials needed, and the structural design entirely.
Who will use the stool — an adult, a child, or both — affects the height, weight capacity, and safety requirements like rails or non-slip features.
Budget determines whether to buy premium hardwood vs. cheaper softwood or plywood, and whether to purchase new tools or work with what is on hand.
The tools already available (e.g. only hand tools vs. a full power-tool setup) directly dictates which joinery methods and designs are feasible.
Whether the stool should match existing kitchen aesthetics — e.g. rustic, modern, painted vs. natural finish — shapes wood choice, finish, and design details.
Knowing the target finished height tells you exactly how tall to build the stool so it solves the actual reach problem in the kitchen.
Whether the user wants a from-scratch design, a specific plan/pattern, or to follow an existing tutorial changes the very first action to take.

gold.taskTitle: Build a simple wooden kitchen step stool
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to build a simple wooden step stool intended for kitchen use.

questions.title: How many steps do you want the stool to have?
questions.description: Determines whether this is a single-step platform, a two-step stool, or something taller — which changes the entire structural design and material quantity.

questions.title: Who will be using this step stool primarily?
questions.description: Identifies whether the primary user is an adult, a child, or both, which drives height, weight capacity, and safety features such as a handle rail.

questions.title: What is your budget for wood and materials?
questions.description: Sets the spending limit, which determines wood species (e.g. pine vs. oak), hardware quality, and finishing products.

questions.title: Which tools do you already have available to use?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user has only hand tools, basic power tools, or a full workshop setup determines which joinery methods and cut techniques are realistic.

questions.title: What look or finish do you want the stool to have?
questions.description: Captures style preferences such as painted, stained, natural, rustic, or modern so the wood choice and finishing steps match the kitchen decor.

questions.title: What height off the ground do you need the top step to reach?
questions.description: Defines the exact finished height required to solve the reach problem, which is the single most critical dimension of the entire build.

questions.title: Do you have a plan or pattern in mind, or need one found?
questions.description: Determines whether the first action is designing from scratch, sourcing a free/paid plan online, or following a specific tutorial the user already has.
